definitions.explanation: The Japanese comma (、), used to separate clauses and items in a sentence. One of the two basic punctuation marks in Japanese writing, alongside the period ({句点|くてん}).

examples.japanese: ⟦ここ→ここ：00961_koko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{読点|とうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}って→打つ：01221_utsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。

examples.english: The meaning of a sentence can change depending on where the comma is placed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{作文|さくぶん}→作文：02884_sakubun⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{読点|とうてん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{句点|くてん}→句点：19157_kuten⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{分|わ}け→使い分け：11559_tsukaiwake⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つけ⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese composition, you must be careful about the proper use of commas and periods.

notes:
The Japanese comma 「、」is called {読点|とうてん}. Used to separate clauses and items in a sentence.

PUNCTUATION PAIR:
- {読点|とうてん} 「、」: comma
- ⟦{句点|くてん}→句点：19157_kuten⟧ 「。」: period
- Together: ⟦{句読点|くとうてん}→句読点：08650_kutouten⟧ (punctuation marks)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読点|とうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to place a comma
- {読点|とうてん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{位置|いち}→位置：11554_ichi⟧: comma placement
- {読点|とうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to insert a comma

USAGE:
Comma placement in Japanese is more flexible than in English. Where to place {読点|とうてん} affects readability and can sometimes change the meaning of a sentence. Horizontal writing uses 「、」while some formal or government documents use 「，」(Western-style comma).
